reviews.comment: Attendance is technically not recorded, but you will miss the slides. 9 homeworks and 2 projects, nothing else. The project is graded harsher than the homework, but miss just a bit of time complexity on the homeworks and you'll get -20 to -30. His lectures are a bit monotonous, but still have a bit of humor here and there. Not a bad choice at all.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible. He curves the class so you will probably pass as long as you do the projects and homework. As far as learning actually goes, virtually none. Got next to nothing out of it. Final project is laughably impossible. Not a good professor.

Great lectures, very accessible outside of the class, and homework are very fair in difficulties. Curves half of the class to an A and other to B as long as you done everything. The only caveat is his projects (very time consuming given he gives us about a month to do them) is bit unclear and didn't give us the grades on it when the semester ends.
I had the deep learning course and the project description and the grading were unclear.

Dr. Jiang is the goat - all lectures are fully recorded and posted online on his website. Super easy to follow and really understandable. You have 1-2 homeworks due every week which are typically pretty easy, as well as 2 very difficult projects. No tests. Start early on the projects and ask for help if you need, and you will be fine.

Top 50% (A), Bottom 50% (B). He teaches very well for you to understand the difficult topics. You can get away with not going to class, just make sure to be on top of the homework and projects. Homework is pretty difficult and can take hours to finish every week, and projects are extremely difficult (start early, there are only two).

I had a great experience with this Prof. He made CSCE 411 very doable and I have had trouble taking this class B4. This might be the toughest CSCE class for the Degree Plan but Prof. Jiang makes it very doable especially considering I took it over the summer. The class for me consisted of 9 homeworks covering various topics and 2 projects. TY Jiang
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Top 50th percentile gets an A, the bottom gets a B. Homework is difficult and projects even more so. You will learn as much as you want. That is, you can easily get away with never showing up to class and scraping by on the assignments, in which case you will learn nothing. He is a great lecturer, so if you show up you will surely learn a lot.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class had three rigorously graded projects instead of exams. He puts a lot of effort into giving his awesome lectures, which are important to attend (although he has online versions available as well from previous years). Assignments require a good understanding of the content (and creativity) to get a good grade. He will help you if you ask.

Dr. Jiang was a pretty good and fair professor. I'd recommend going to office hours, where he explains the homework and project concepts pretty easily. This class had no exams. However, there were 9 homeworks (60% of grade) and only 2 projects (40%). The top half of the class got an A and the bottom half got a B (assuming you did all the work).
reviews.ratingTags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I am taking his 629 for my fast track and I love every lecture. His lecture slides convey concepts super clearly and you can see the effort put into making them. Our grade is based on 50% homework and 50% random quiz-tests. The tests are certainly difficult, but everybody strugles together. They can take at least 20 minutes and are honestly fun.

No live lectures. Had to watch youtube videos every week. To ask questions you had to go to his office hours. We had a one-semester-long project which was to solve 40 questions. It took about 10,000 pages to write all the code, explanation, efficiency, correctness. The whole class is graded on that project. Didn't learn anything.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Analysis of Algorithm One of the best professor in the CS department at TAMU. He explains theoretical concepts in a crystal clear manner. His exams are tough and that decide the final grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is superrrr sweet. Attendance was never taken, but he gives good examples in class so attending made life easier. Tests are open book and open notes, and it always helped to have my homework out during the tests because he gave similar problems. He was very caring, and everyone I know made an A in his class just by trying.

Dr. Jiang was a very passionate professor. He seemed to enjoy his material quite a bit and that is always reassuring. I think his lectures were kind of hard to follow but as long as you actively complete the coursework I don't believe you'll fail. He was nice and also energetic. He struggled with a clear grading curriculum though.
Professor Jiang, Makes it really comfortable for any one to ask question and takes all the time to make everyone understand, with Suitable examples
The most recommend in computer science.
